images.title: Three faces meet at each corner
images.purpose: Compare a net of a regular tetrahedron with four triangles around one point, which cannot fold into one.
images.composition: Two shapes side by side on white with no panel borders: a net on the left, a non-net on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left: one large equilateral triangle split by joining its midpoints into 4 equal equilateral triangles, filled green #009E73 with thin dark outlines; the midpoint of the big triangle's left side, where three of the small triangles meet, is ringed in reddish purple #CC79A7 with the label '3 meet here', and under the shape the label 'net'. Right: 4 equal equilateral triangles of the same size all sharing one common point and fanned side by side (covering two thirds of a full turn), filled vermilion #D55E00; the shared point is ringed in reddish purple with the label '4 meet here', and under the shape the label 'not a net'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A regular tetrahedron has 3 faces at every corner, so 4 triangles around one point cannot fold into it.
images.description: Compare a net of a regular tetrahedron with four triangles around one point, which cannot fold into one.
images.context: One clean concept image for T8.C1.
images.teaching_notes: Left ring: a midpoint of the big triangle, where the centre triangle and two corner triangles meet.

image_decisions.why: The reason a net fails is a count at one corner; two shapes side by side show it.
